 Details have surfaced online about the postponement of the second trailer for the Resident Evil remake. 
 Evgen Kovalov 
 GAMES 
 November 08, 2026 
 Views: 10722 
 Capcom has adjusted its marketing and production plans for the next major project in the Resident Evil franchise. According to information published by respected industry insider Dusk Golem, the company initially planned to reveal the second official trailer for the remake sometime recently. However, internal management decided to postpone the reveal of the video and give the development team additional time to systematically work on the game. The publisher chose to take its time with media activity surrounding the project to ensure the final product fully meets the studio's high quality standards.
 The main reason for postponing the planned demo was the developers' desire to use the allocated time to thoroughly refine the project. The developers focused on fixing minor and medium-sized technical issues, optimizing the code, and thoroughly polishing various aspects of the environment. Studio management concluded that a hasty public demonstration of a working build could negatively impact the overall perception of this reimagining of the cult classic. The additional production weeks will allow the developers to thoroughly fine-tune the visual elements, lighting, and basic mechanics of interaction with the surrounding world.
 In recent years, Capcom has been paying increased attention to the technological state of its releases on PC and modern home consoles, striving to completely eliminate stability issues at launch. This pragmatic approach to the transfer of promotional materials confirms the publisher's intention to present the most complete and polished build possible. The exact timing of the second trailer's presentation remains unknown, but industry experts anticipate the next reveal will coincide with major upcoming gaming exhibitions, where the project will receive maximum attention from industry press and audiences.
